:::{#thm-rank-subadditive}
#### Rank is subadditive

For $m \times n$ matrices $\matr{A}$ and $\matr{B}$,

$$
\operatorname{rank}(\matr{A} + \matr{B})
\le \operatorname{rank}(\matr{A}) + \operatorname{rank}(\matr{B}).
$$

:::

::: proof

**$\mathcal{C}(\matr{A} + \matr{B}) \subseteq \mathcal{C}(\matr{A}) + \mathcal{C}(\matr{B})$.**
Any vector of $\mathcal{C}(\matr{A} + \matr{B})$ is
$(\matr{A} + \matr{B})\,\vecf{x}$ for some $\vecf{x} \in \reals^n$
(@def-column-space), and
$(\matr{A} + \matr{B})\,\vecf{x} = \matr{A} \vecf{x} + \matr{B} \vecf{x}$
(@thm-matmul-distrib, with $\vecf{x}$ as an $n \times 1$ matrix),
a vector of $\mathcal{C}(\matr{A})$ plus a vector of $\mathcal{C}(\matr{B})$.

**Compare dimensions.**
All the sets involved are subspaces of $\reals^m$
(@thm-column-space-span, @thm-sum-intersection-subspace), so

$$
\ba
\operatorname{rank}(\matr{A} + \matr{B})
&= \dim\paren{\mathcal{C}(\matr{A} + \matr{B})}
&& \text{(@thm-rank-dim)}
\\
&\le \dim\paren{\mathcal{C}(\matr{A}) + \mathcal{C}(\matr{B})}
&& \text{(the containment, and part 2 of @thm-dim-bound)}
\\
&\le \dim\paren{\mathcal{C}(\matr{A})} + \dim\paren{\mathcal{C}(\matr{B})}
&& \text{(@cor-dim-subadditive)}
\\
&= \operatorname{rank}(\matr{A}) + \operatorname{rank}(\matr{B}).
&& \text{(@thm-rank-dim)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-rank-subadditive}
#### Subadditivity with equality and without

Let
$\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$
and
$\matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$.
Each has one nonzero column and one zero column.
The nonzero column on its own is linearly independent
($c\,\vecf{v} = \vzero_2$ with $\vecf{v} \ne \vzero_2$ forces $c = 0$),
and the two columns together are not,
since $1$ times the zero column is $\vzero_2$;
so each matrix has rank $1$ (@def-rank).
By the same argument, $-\matr{A}$ has rank $1$.

- $\matr{A} + \matr{B}$ is the $2 \times 2$ identity matrix, which has rank $2$
  (@exm-rank-nullity),
  so the bound $2 \le 1 + 1$ holds with equality.
- $\matr{A} + (-\matr{A})$ is the $2 \times 2$ zero matrix,
  which has rank $0$:
  any nonempty list of its columns contains $\vzero_2$,
  and $1 \cd \vzero_2 = \vzero_2$.
  So the bound $0 \le \operatorname{rank}(\matr{A}) + \operatorname{rank}(-\matr{A}) = 1 + 1$
  is strict.

:::
